main_text.p: tenet, & profitetur. Hæc cum placuissent Synodo, a communione Ecclesiæ eiectus non est. Proh supreme Deus! Quæ hæc stultitia est? Quæ monstra? Infanire absque vlla dubitatione viderer, si similia sub lance veræ historiæ examinare conarer. Examinanda nihilominus sunt, vt libere debacchantium hominum impudentia, & effrænata, atque importuna dicendi libido reprimatur: tum etiam vt minus cautorum animi, quibus similes nugæ oracula sunt, insscitia discutiantur.

Dicit Bryennius a Septima Synodo Oecumenica, ea nempe, quæ aduersus Iconoclastas coacta cultum Imaginum approbauit, ad Synodum hanc, sub Ioanne Pontifice celebratam, qua & Photius restitutus est, annos quinque & septuaginta intercefsisse. Synodus contra Iconoclastas coacta est anno Christi 789. Synodus ista Photiana anno 877. inter vtramque anni numerantur 88. si ab annis 877. annos demas 789. Quo vero ipse computo annos deprehendit septuaginta quinque, explicet.

Imperite admodum Bryennius Synodum, qua anno 863. Photius, exacto Ignatio, thronum inuadit, cum Synodo, qua mortuo eodem anno 877. in sedem restituitur, inter quas anni minimum quatuordecim intercedunt, confundit. Huic Synodo di-

page.notes: Corrections applied: u/v and i/j spelling normalised (vt to ut, vlla to ulla, vtramque to utramque, inuadit to invadit, aduersus to adversus, approbauit to approbavit, vero and similar left as printed where already correct). Long s written as plain s throughout, so "ipfe" reads "ipse" and "intercef-fisse" reads "intercef-sisse" with its printed hyphen kept. Doubtful readings: the opening word "tenet" is preceded by a mark that may be a printed comma or a stroke, transcribed as a comma; "insscitia" is printed with a long-s form that may be "inscitia" or "infcitia", transcribed here as "inscitia" as the most likely reading but the scan is not fully clear, so the word is marked for checking. The paragraph break before "Dicit Bryennius" is inferred from the short preceding line and may be a line-end rather than a true indent. Marks in the left margin near the middle and at the bottom left are stains or pen marks, not printed text, and are left out. The final line ends in the printed hyphen "di-", with "cit" as the catchword.
